root_cause.text: In the ab8500 power-supply charger probe path, `devm_request_threaded_irq()` was called before devm registration of the `power_supply` object, so managed-resource teardown order allowed the IRQ handler to run with an uninitialized or already freed `power_supply` handle used by `power_supply_changed()`.
root_cause.evidence: The patch moves the entire “Request interrupts” block from before `di->usb_chg.psy` registration to after it, and the CVE/commit message explicitly states that requesting IRQs first causes reverse-order `devm_` cleanup to free/unregister the `power_supply` before the IRQ handler is removed, creating a race where `power_supply_changed()` is called on a freed or uninitialized handle.

intent_record.intent_summary: Remove charger IRQ registration from probe so this code path no longer installs those interrupts or fails on their request.
intent_record.what: The probe function removes an entire loop that iterated over ab8500_charger_irq, fetched each IRQ by name with platform_get_irq_byname(), requested each threaded IRQ with devm_request_threaded_irq(), and logged success or failure before returning on errors.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the driver no longer requests or registers any of these charger interrupts during probe, so their handlers will not be installed from this code path and probe will no longer fail because of missing or failed IRQ requests in this section.

intent_record.intent_summary: Request and validate all charger IRQs during probe so the driver handles hardware events correctly and fails initialization if interrupt setup is unavailable.
intent_record.what: A new interrupt-request block was added to ab8500_charger_probe() after successful USB power-supply registration: it loops over ab8500_charger_irq[], retrieves each IRQ with platform_get_irq_byname(), returns immediately on lookup failure, requests each IRQ with devm_request_threaded_irq() using the corresponding threaded handler and IRQF_SHARED | IRQF_NO_SUSPEND | IRQF_ONESHOT flags, logs an error and returns on request failure, and emits a debug log on success.
intent_record.how: At probe time, the charger driver now registers all named charger interrupts before continuing initialization. This enables the driver's interrupt handlers to receive charger-related events during runtime, and it aborts probing early if any required IRQ is missing or cannot be requested, preventing the device from running without its interrupt support.

relevance_review.reason: The vulnerability is caused by IRQ registration in probe occurring before the power_supply devm registration, creating a teardown-order/use-after-free risk in the IRQ handler. Removing charger IRQ registration from probe directly eliminates that problematic registration path and its handler exposure.

The change directly concerns requesting charger IRQs during probe, which is the operation at the heart of the root cause. Since the vulnerability stems from calling devm_request_threaded_irq() before power_supply devm registration, IRQ setup ordering in probe is directly related.

candidates.rationale: This is the key operation that registers managed IRQ handlers during probe before the power_supply object is devm-registered, creating the teardown-order bug where the handler can run while using an uninitialized or freed power_supply.
This loop causes all charger IRQs to be requested in probe at the vulnerable point in initialization, making the ordering issue systematic across all handlers.
This is part of the probe-time IRQ setup path that enables the subsequent vulnerable registration before power_supply registration is complete.

vuln_statements.explanation: This statement performs the managed IRQ registration during probe. Because it occurs before the devm-managed power_supply registration, managed-resource teardown can leave the IRQ handler able to run while its power_supply dependency is uninitialized or already freed, leading to the use in power_supply_changed().
This loop drives the probe-time registration of all charger IRQs at the vulnerable point in initialization, making the incorrect managed-resource ordering apply across all handlers.

bic_trace_step.code_snippet:
commit 1c1f13a006ed0d71bb5664c8b7e3e77a28da3beb
Author: Linus Walleij <linusw@kernel.org>
Date:   Sun May 23 00:50:39 2021 +0200

    power: supply: ab8500: Move to componentized binding
    
    The driver has problems with the different components of

bic_trace_step.reason: The diff is sufficient because it shows the relevant ordering inside `ab8500_charger_probe()`. The root cause is that `devm_request_threaded_irq()` happens before devm registration of the `power_supply` object, which can make managed teardown free the power supply before the IRQ is released, allowing the IRQ handler to call `power_supply_changed()` on an invalid/uninitialized handle. That exact ordering is present here: in `ab8500_charger_probe()` the code first requests IRQs using `ret = devm_request_threaded_irq(dev, irq, NULL, ab8500_charger_irq[i].isr, ...)` in the loop added near `/* Request interrupts */`. Only later does it register the power supplies with `di->ac_chg.psy = devm_power_supply_register(dev, &ab8500_ac_chg_desc, &ac_psy_cfg);` and `di->usb_chg.psy = devm_power_supply_register(dev, &ab8500_usb_chg_desc, &usb_psy_cfg);`. Because both are devm-managed, teardown occurs in reverse registration order, so the later-registered power supplies are released before the earlier IRQs, matching the vulnerable condition described. There is no compensating logic here to ensure IRQs are torn down before the power supplies or to defer IRQ registration until after `devm_power_supply_register()`. Therefore the vulnerable construct is present and the fix is not yet present.

bic_trace_step.reason: The snippet is sufficient because it shows the full relevant ordering inside `ab8500_charger_probe()`: IRQs are requested, power supplies are registered, and later teardown is delegated to devm/component paths. The root cause is present here. In `ab8500_charger_probe()`, interrupts are requested early with `ret = devm_request_threaded_irq(dev, irq, NULL, ab8500_charger_irq[i].isr, ... , di);` in the loop added near the top of probe, before the power supply objects are created. Only later does the code register the supplies with `di->ac_chg.psy = devm_power_supply_register(dev, &ab8500_ac_chg_desc, &ac_psy_cfg);` and `di->usb_chg.psy = devm_power_supply_register(dev, &ab8500_usb_chg_desc, &usb_psy_cfg);`. That matches the described bug condition: `devm_request_threaded_irq()` comes before devm registration of the `power_supply` objects, so on managed teardown the power supplies may be released before the IRQs, allowing an IRQ handler to run and use `di->*_chg.psy` in callbacks such as `power_supply_changed()` after it is uninitialized/freed. The fix is not present because the ordering is still unsafe: the code did not move `devm_power_supply_register()` before `devm_request_threaded_irq()`, nor otherwise disable/synchronize IRQs before devm power-supply teardown.

bic_trace_step.reason: The function body is sufficient because it clearly shows the ordering of power_supply registration and IRQ registration. The root cause describes a bug where `devm_request_threaded_irq()` was called before devm registration of the `power_supply` object, creating a managed-resource teardown ordering problem. In this snippet, the code does not use `devm_request_threaded_irq()` at all; instead it uses plain `request_threaded_irq()` at lines 2943-2945 and manually frees IRQs on error at lines 2980-2984. Also, both power supplies are registered before IRQs are requested: `power_supply_register(di->dev, &di->ac_chg.psy);` at line 2897 and `power_supply_register(di->dev, &di->usb_chg.psy);` at line 2904, while IRQ registration happens later starting at line 2941. Therefore the specific vulnerable construct described in the root cause—managed IRQ registration occurring before managed power_supply registration—is absent here, so `has_bug` is false. However, the fix as described is also not present in the sense that there is no devm-based corrected ordering of `devm_power_supply_register()` before `devm_request_threaded_irq()`; instead this version uses non-devm registration APIs, so `is_fixed` is false for that specific fix pattern.
